h1: Digital marketing services agencies sell, and what they cost
metaTitle: What Are the Digital Marketing Services on Offer?
metaDescription: The fourteen digital marketing services agencies actually sell, each with an Indian price band, so you can build a scope instead of buying a bundle.
answer: Digital marketing services are the individual line items an agency sells — technical SEO, content, link building, local SEO, Google Ads, paid social, organic social, influencer, email, CRO, analytics, creative, web build and reporting. In India each runs roughly ₹15,000 to ₹1,50,000 a month, and most proposals bundle them so you can't see the split.
takeaways: There are fourteen real line items. A "package" is those line items with the prices removed.
Ask for any proposal **itemised with hours or deliverables per line**. The refusal is the answer.
A small brand needs four of the fourteen, and can genuinely run on **₹60,000–₹1,00,000 a month** all in.
Four of the fourteen need a specialist. Buying them from a generalist is how you pay full price for a placeholder.

body: Almost every digital marketing proposal in India is built from the same fourteen components. The names get rearranged, the pricing gets bundled, but underneath it's this list.
The bands below are typical Indian market rates for the work done competently — not the cheapest quote you can find, and not agency-of-record rates in Bandra. All exclude GST and exclude media spend.

callout.title: Why the bands are this wide
callout.body: Four things move every number here: who does the work, whether production is included, how competitive your category is, and whether media spend is bundled into the fee. A quote is not comparable to another quote until you know all four.

sections.h2: Which line items get bundled to hide margin
body: Bundling isn't automatically dishonest. Some services genuinely belong together — on-page SEO without technical SEO is redecorating a building with a cracked foundation.
But bundling is also the standard way to hide a thin line item behind a fat one. Four patterns come up repeatedly in the proposals founders forward to us:
bullets: **"Content and SEO" as one number.** Content is the expensive part. If the split isn't stated, you often find the SEO is four hours a month of keyword tracking and the rest is articles you could have commissioned for a third of the price.
**"Social media management" covering organic and paid.** Two different jobs, two different skill sets, and the paid half usually carries a percentage-of-spend fee buried in the same line.
**"Reporting and strategy" as a headline deliverable.** Reporting is a by-product of the work, not a service. When it appears as a priced line item at ₹20,000 a month, you are paying for a dashboard.

**Media spend folded into the retainer.** The worst one. A ₹1,50,000 "performance marketing" fee that includes ₹90,000 of ad budget is a ₹60,000 service, and you cannot tell whether the media is being marked up.

callout.title: The one question that unbundles any proposal
callout.body: "Can you re-send this with each line item priced separately, and media spend on its own row?" A confident agency does it in an afternoon. Watch what happens instead — hedging here predicts everything about the next twelve months.

sections.h2: The minimum viable scope for a small brand
body: You do not need fourteen services. Most brands under ₹5 crore in revenue need four, and adding the other ten early is the most common way to spend a year's budget on activity instead of customers.
Here's a defensible starting scope, and roughly what it should cost:

callout.title: Where that lands
callout.body: Between ₹60,000 and ₹1,00,000 a month once the setup is behind you. Below ₹40,000 a month in total, you're usually better off doing the work yourself with a good freelancer for the technical bits — there's a realistic plan for that in [how to do digital marketing on a small budget](/answers/how-to-do-digital-marketing).

sections.h2: The four that need a specialist, not a generalist
body: Ten of the fourteen can be done well by a good generalist team. Four cannot, and they're the four most often thrown into a package as a bullet point.
If these matter to your business, buy them from someone who does only them:
numbered: **Technical SEO on a large or JavaScript-heavy site.** Rendering, crawl budget, faceted navigation, migrations. Getting this wrong doesn't underperform, it removes you from the index. A generalist who "also does technical" is a real risk on a site above a few thousand URLs.

**Digital PR and link building.** This is a media relations job wearing an SEO badge. Done by a generalist it becomes guest posts on sites that exist only to sell guest posts, which is a penalty with a delay on it.
**Analytics and server-side tracking.** Event design, consent handling, CRM stitching. Half the reporting disputes we see between clients and agencies are actually a tracking bug nobody owned.

**Conversion rate optimisation.** Requires enough traffic for a valid test and someone who understands what a valid test is. Below roughly a thousand conversions a month, most "CRO" is redesigning pages and calling random variation a win.

sections.h2: How to turn a bundle quote into something comparable
body: Three proposals with three different bundles cannot be compared. Force them into the same shape first — it takes an hour and it's the highest-return hour in the whole buying process.
numbered: **Rewrite every quote onto the fourteen-line list above.** Anything the agency includes goes on a row; anything they don't, leave blank. The blanks are the negotiation.
**Pull media spend out of every fee.** Compare service fees to service fees. Ask explicitly whether media is marked up — some agencies take a percentage of your ad budget on top of management.
**Ask for deliverables with numbers.** Four articles or twelve? Two links or ten? "Ongoing optimisation" is not a deliverable, it's a word.

**Ask who does each line, by name and seniority.** The people who win the pitch are frequently not the people who do the work. This is the single most common complaint founders bring us about a previous agency.

**Ask what happens if it doesn't work.** Most contracts have no answer. That's the question that separates the field, and it's covered further in [how to compare SEO proposals](/answers/how-to-compare-seo-proposals).

sections.h2: What we sell, and what's inside the number
body: We sell three of the fourteen properly rather than all fourteen thinly, and we publish the prices so you can do the comparison above without a call.

SEO runs from **₹75,000/mo**, with smaller sites from **₹40,000/mo** — that covers technical, on-page, content and link work with reporting as a by-product rather than a line item. Organic social and content is **₹30,000 / ₹50,000 / ₹70,000** a month. Performance marketing is **₹40,000 / ₹75,000 / ₹1,50,000** a month, with ad spend billed separately at zero markup. Bundled, that's ₹99,000 for SEO plus social, ₹75,000 for social plus performance, or ₹1,75,000 for all three. Everything is ex-GST, month-to-month after the first quarter, 30 days' notice, and you keep every asset.

The part that isn't a line item: we freeze your trailing-90-day qualified organic lead count on day one, and if we haven't beaten it in 90 days we keep working free until we do. Not a ranking position — nobody controls Google's index — a number from your own business, agreed before anyone starts. It's also why we take three clients a month. See [what's in the SEO retainer](/seo) or the full [pricing](/pricing).

faqs.q: What services does a digital marketing agency offer?
faqs.a: Fourteen recurring line items: technical SEO, on-page SEO, content, link building and digital PR, local SEO, Google Ads, paid social, organic social, influencer, email, CRO, analytics, creative production and web build. Packages are these items with the individual prices removed.

faqs.q: How much do digital marketing services cost in India?
faqs.a: Individual line items typically run ₹15,000 to ₹1,50,000 a month each. A workable four-line scope for a small brand lands between ₹60,000 and ₹1,00,000 a month plus a setup cost. Below ₹40,000 a month total, a freelancer plus your own time usually beats a diluted agency retainer.

faqs.q: Should I buy a package or individual services?
faqs.a: Individual services, priced separately, then combined if the maths works. A package isn't inherently worse value — but you can't tell whether it is, which is the point of the packaging. Ask for the itemised version and compare like with like.

faqs.q: Which digital marketing service gives the fastest return?
faqs.a: Email to an existing list, then paid search. Both can produce measurable revenue inside a fortnight. SEO and content take three to six months but keep paying after you stop spending, which is a different kind of return rather than a slower version of the same one.

faqs.q: Do agencies mark up ad spend?
faqs.a: Some do, either as a percentage of media on top of the management fee or by folding spend into a single retainer number so it isn't visible. Ask directly and get it in writing. We bill media separately at zero markup, which makes the fee legible.

faqs.q: What's the difference between digital marketing services and SEO services?
faqs.a: SEO is one channel inside digital marketing, covering technical, on-page, content and off-page work for search. Digital marketing services include SEO plus paid media, social, email, creative and analytics. An SEO-only agency goes deeper on one; a digital agency covers more, usually less deeply.
